facts.claim: 作者把骨架类笑话放在章节最前，第一条就用 guts 同时指“内脏”与“胆量”的双关收尾
facts.quote: Why don’t skeletons fight each other? They don’t have the guts.

facts.claim: 紧接着是“鬼屋”第一人称段子：说者自称住了四百年没见过鬼，反转点是说者自己才是鬼
facts.quote: My housemates keep saying our house is haunted. That’s ridiculous – I’ve lived here for 400 years and never seen a ghost.

facts.claim: 鬼魂类笑话靠同音替换（ear → eeriest）把“听力好”字面化，机制是一条谐音梗
facts.quote: What kind of ghost has the best hearing? The eeriest.

facts.claim: 吸血鬼/德古拉一类被归在“脖子”意象上，用 neck-romancer 谐音 necromancer 作笑点
facts.quote: Why does Dracula like biting women’s throats? Because he’s a neck-romancer.

facts.claim: 作者也收“职业 + 鬼”的复合词笑话，把 ghost writer 当成字面身份来问
facts.quote: What’s the spookiest kind of author? A ghost writer.

facts.claim: 狼人笑话用拖长的嚎叫拼写收尾，把变身恐怖降格成一句含糊的自我安慰
facts.quote: I used to be a werewolf but I’m alright noooooooooooooooow.

facts.claim: 全章以一则吸血蝙蝠长故事压轴，短笑话清单由此切换到一句话长段子
facts.quote: A colony of vampire bats are struggling to find enough blood, and keep going out hunting and coming back with no success.

facts.claim: 长故事的落点是把“看不见”当证据：蝙蝠指着一根灯柱说自己撞上去，血由此而来
facts.quote: He lands in a tree and says, ‘Do you see that lamp post?’ The other bats nod hungrily. ‘Well, I didn’t.’

relations.relation: 两条都拿“身体缺席”作字面答案：一个没有 guts，一个能被看穿，双关都落在“鬼没有实体”上
relations.quote: Why are ghosts such unconvincing liars? Because you can see right through them.

relations.relation: 同属“把一个常用词换成鬼词根”的造词法：ear→eeriest 是同音，writer→ghost writer 是复合
relations.quote: What kind of ghost has the best hearing? The eeriest.

relations.relation: 两条狼人笑话都把恐怖形象日常化：一条用拖长元音模拟嚎叫，一条让妈妈叫狼人梳脸而不是梳头
relations.quote: ‘Mum, am I a werewolf?’ ‘Oh, stop asking questions and comb your face.’

relations.pair: 短笑话清单 / 结尾蝙蝠长故事
relations.relation: 章末的蝙蝠故事与前面的单句笑话形成长短对照，作者用它当压轴而不是再列一条短梗
relations.quote: He lands in a tree and says, ‘Do you see that lamp post?’

numbers.meaning: 鬼屋段子里说者自称在这屋里住了四百年，暗示他就是鬼
numbers.quote: I’ve lived here for 400 years and never seen a ghost.

numbers.meaning: 钟敲十三下，笑话给的建议是“该换钟了”，用不存在的时刻当由头
numbers.quote: What time is it when the clock strikes 13? Time to get a new clock.

numbers.meaning: 弗兰肯斯坦的怪物骑三轮车，靠“庞大恐怖 + 三轮”的落差出笑点
numbers.quote: What’s enormous, terrifying and has three wheels? Frankenstein’s monster riding a tricycle.
